A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DC-PnPDP work. Text, equations, tables, figures and all appendices are readable. Retained material can be matched despite substantial additions and relocation of the original main results.

before.justification: v1 reports original CT and fastMRI knee reconstruction experiments, component ablations, spectral diagnostics and inference-budget results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and reports additional brain MRI, cross-dataset CT, natural-image restoration, residual and runtime results.

M1.justification: The core DC-PnPDP updates and diffusion-prior architecture are retained. Appendix B.6 adds a procedural adaptation that inserts SH into DDNM by replacing its standard DDIM re-noising step, although the authors present this as a scope diagnostic.

E1.justification: v2 adds fastMRI brain reconstruction, AAPM and DeepLesion CT evaluation, and natural-image Gaussian deblurring, motion deblurring and 4x super-resolution. AbdomenCT-1K and fastMRI knee coverage remain; knee results move to Appendix B.1.

E2.justification: SITCOM joins the main quantitative comparison, and Appendix B.5 introduces the supervised ProCT comparator, substantially broadening comparison methods. The original four diffusion baselines remain in Table 3. Main CT qualitative panels replace DAPS with SITCOM, while DAPS remains evaluated elsewhere.

E3.justification: v2 adds recommended-budget comparisons: 100 NFEs for DDNM/DDS/DiffPIR, reported budgets of 5x200 for DAPS and 50x10 for SITCOM, and 50/100 NFEs for DC-PnPDP. The original uniform 50-NFE protocol remains in Table 3. New designs include a 200-slice brain subset, sweeps to 1000 NFEs, residual measurements and batch-10 runtime profiling.

E4.justification: The original component ablation and spectral diagnostic remain. v2 adds measurement-residual and dual-state trajectories, extends the budget analysis to examine high-budget plateaus, profiles runtime and memory, tests ProCT under in-domain/OOD conditions, and examines SH transfer to DDNM.

E5.justification: Unlike v1's point estimates, v2 Table 6 reports mean ± standard deviation for natural-image restoration. The aggregation unit, repeated-run counts and seeds are unspecified, so this establishes additional variability reporting, not additional independent runs.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1 is preserved numerically as v2 Table 3, and the component ablation is unchanged. v2 adds substantial results under its expanded protocols: Table 1 reports LACT PSNR 39.46 versus DiffPIR's 34.70 at 100 NFEs, and brain AF=10 PSNR 30.91 versus SITCOM's 28.67 under their reported budgets. Runtime, cross-dataset CT, natural-image and extended-budget findings are also new; these are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The explanation of Eq. (13) corrects the Fourier normalization convention from a unitary DFT to an unnormalized FFT, making the stated HW scaling consistent. The spectral-consistency proposition and bootstrap/fixed-point assumptions, theorems and proofs otherwise retain their substance; appendices B–D become C–E.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claimed theoretical guarantee of convergence to the exact data manifold with progressive agreement between data-consistency and prior variables. The efficiency discussion emphasizes inference efficiency. The central dual-feedback, SH, bias-reduction and superior-fidelity contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an SNR/geometry explanation for differing CT, knee and brain gains, interprets high-budget behavior and residual trajectories, and explains computational tradeoffs. It explicitly separates PSNR-versus-NFE evidence from formal optimization convergence, qualifies the supervised comparison's scope, and discusses SH applicability beyond dual-coupled solvers.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 substantially expands baseline documentation with task-specific 10-slice validation, DAPS Langevin parameters and separate budget configurations, SITCOM optimization settings, and the MRI closed-form data-consistency implementation. Runtime hardware, batch size and memory details are added. The CT training recipe and code URL remain, although some new benchmark setups lack dataset/sample specifications.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section substantially expands positioning against PnP-ADMM convergence, adaptation and stochastic methods, plus concurrent diffusion/ADMM approaches. It explicitly distinguishes SH from AC-DC's Langevin correction, stochastic generative PnP, dual-ascent diffusion and colored re-noising. These are substantive additions beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the empirical narrative into recommended-budget main results and controlled-budget appendix results, adds a dedicated Related Work section and structured diagnostic/discussion subsections, and rewrites the MRI and efficiency discussions. Much of the method and theoretical prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The main table gains budget columns and separate DC-PnPDP rows; the original table and knee figure move to the appendix. Main qualitative examples are replaced, Figure 4 is redrawn over a logarithmic budget range to 1000 NFEs, and new runtime, residual, ProCT and natural-image displays are added. Appendix CT panels are also replaced and include SITCOM.

improvement.justification: v1 supported efficiency mainly through uniform 50-NFE comparisons and a short budget sweep. v2 preserves that control while testing recommended and larger budgets, adding residual diagnostics and measured runtime, and clarifying positioning against closely related work. These changes substantially strengthen evidence for the central benefits. Some added experiments remain underspecified, Tables 1 and 3 contain unreconciled 50-NFE CT scores, and convergence claims remain incompletely qualified, but the overall gain in validation and transparency is substantial.
